note: THE PROOF-OF-PROGRESS LEDGER for the BN4 legs -- the speedrun route's
FIRST three completions (bn4.1, bn4.2, bn4.3), of which only leg-bn4.1 has
ever been measured.
FIRST MEASUREMENT (2026-08-29). Before this file, `leg-bn4.1` had never run
past ten virtual minutes: every run in runs/ was a smoke with lastT between
45s and 600s, there was no `bench:sim:leg-bn4.1` script and no BN4 lane. The
route's own first leg was its least-covered one. These numbers are the first
evidence it has.
WHAT THIS LEG IS. A genuinely fresh BN4: 8 GB home, $1,000, no Source-Files.
Singularity is node-native, which is why the route starts here and why
nothing is injected. BN4 is also the hardest possible opening --
WorldDaemonDifficulty 3 puts the daemon at hacking 9000 (three times BN1)
while ScriptHackMoney 0.2 x ServerMaxMoney 0.1125 leaves hacking earning
~2% of BN1, HackExpGain is 0.4, and hacknet/crime/company money are 0.05 /
0.2 / 0.1. Stocks and coding contracts are the only unnerfed money channels.
NO LIKE-FOR-LIKE TARGET EXISTS. The historical 17d run
(spec/strategy/speedrun-benchmark.md) did 4.1 in 14h15m, but it entered BN4
holding SF1.1 earned in a 21-minute manual BN1. This leg enters with
nothing, so 14h15m is a reference point, not a target to miss.
Each entry is the BEST result we have actually observed on that profile, not
a target and not a guess. Some of these numbers are FAILURES; they are here
because a failure you have measured is the starting point of the next
improvement.
RULES.
1. Only ever move a number in the improving direction, and only from a run
you actually observed. Never relax one to make a red run green.
2. `timeToGoalHours` and `firstInstallHours` improve DOWNWARD.
`augmentationsAt`, `installs` and `reached` improve UPWARD.
3. `provenance` pins the simulator semantics these numbers were measured
under. Bumping SIMULATOR_MODEL_VERSION or the vendored commit changes
what the simulator DOES, so old numbers stop being comparable.
4. Say which KIND of change moved a number. A semantics change makes old
numbers incomparable; a controller change moves them because that is
the point. The 2026-08-30 entry is the second kind twice over -- a
strategy commit and a harness fix -- and neither touched the model.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE. A 3-seed 24h batch runs concurrently and costs about 27
wall minutes end to end:
bun run long bn4                             # the validity smoke, 15 vmin
bun run bench:sim:leg-bn4.1                  # the benchmark, seeds 1-3
bun run sim -- --profile leg-bn4.1 --seed 3 --horizon 72h --compact --perf
bun run sim -- --profile leg-bn4.1 --seed 2 --horizon 24h --compact --perf \
--cost --cost-every 30s        # RSS, live processes and throughput per sample
SIM_COST_DETAIL=8 ...            # + heap census and per-interval ns calls

openDefects.what: `--perf` (telemetry off) and the ordinary telemetry build played measurably different games from the same seed, which AGENTS.md forbids: 'A --perf build must be behaviourally identical to a telemetry build -- only quieter.' On leg-bn4.1 seed 3 at a 30h horizon, --perf reached 6 installs / 35 augs / hacking 867 / 16.12h route ETA while telemetry on reached 2 installs / 24 augs / hacking 379 / 151.18h.
openDefects.cause: `initTelemetry` built its run id from `Math.random()` (game/lib/telemetry.ts). The simulator replaces `Math.random` with the run's SEEDED stream (sim/realm/timers.ts:168), so that single draw shifted every later random number in the process. Each mode stayed internally deterministic, which is why the divergence read as a strategy result rather than as a seed shift.
openDefects.fix: The run id is now derived from `shortIdentity(identity.install.id)` -- state the run already holds, no RNG, still unique. Verified: telemetry-on and --perf now agree EXACTLY at a 30h horizon, prestiges [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 19.706, 21.363] and identical installs/augs/hacking/trades/route ETA. Pinned by tests/telemetry-client.test.ts, which asserts initTelemetry takes ZERO draws and fails on the old line.
openDefects.impactOnRecordedEvidence: NONE, and this is the important correction. The unshifted stream is the --perf one, and every route-leg baseline in this repo was recorded under --perf, so no recorded number moves. The bug was also inert in the real game, where `Math.random` is not seeded. What it broke was comparability: any simulator run taken with telemetry on -- a UI-attached run, a dashboard session -- was not comparable to the --perf benchmarks it would be read against.

openDefects.what: DIAGNOSED. leg-bn4.1 does not stall on strategy -- the CONTROLLER LOOP STOPS. At t~21.9h the ns-proxy resident `nsp` needs a 162.1 GB placement that no host in the fleet can hold, and `NsProxy.#respawn` (game/lib/ns-proxy.ts:528-605) retries it in an unbounded `for(;;)` loop. The controller awaits that call, so it never completes another pass: every telemetry topic goes silent at 21.89-21.97h with hours of horizon left, no installs happen, no augmentations are bought, and the published route ETA freezes at its last value. The run stays `valid` with no crashes and no unmodeled calls, because nothing actually fails -- it waits forever.
evidence: The run prints it: sim.result `output` carries `WARNING: ns resident nsp cannot be PLACED at all (needs 162.1GB) -- retrying; no host in the fleet has that much free.` and the same at 82.1 GB earlier.
Every topic stops publishing at once, 2.1 hours before the horizon: progression 21.97h, arbitration 21.97h, factions 21.95h, career 21.91h, player 21.89h, endgame.route 21.70h, against a 24h horizon.

The engine is fine -- engineCycles=432000 is exactly 24h of 200ms cycles. Already-dispatched work continues without the controller: charisma 575 -> 711 and money $54.3b -> $56.6b after it goes silent, while hacking (+12), installs, augmentations and stock trades are frozen.

Reproduced by a probe matching the CLI exactly (label, profile, experiment, goFidelity, allowBitNodeCompletion): prestiges [1.067, 5.036, 8.742, 11.561, 19.706, 21.363], identical to bench:sim:leg-bn4.1.
openDefects.suspect: Not yet isolated, and note it must be re-established under whichever mode survives openDefects/perf-build-plays-a-different-game: the freeze above is a property of the --perf trajectory. A filtered telemetry-on probe of the same leg did NOT reproduce it -- there faction reputation accrues steadily (The Black Hand 3,188 -> 162,927 rep over 19.2h-24.25h) toward a 7-augmentation package -- but that probe is a different trajectory for the same reason.
openDefects.nextStep: Two candidate fixes, and the choice is a design decision in a load-bearing subsystem rather than a bolt-on. (1) Chunk the declared union: unlike a single indivisible call, a 160 GB union of many calls can be split into placeable batches, which is the direct fix. (2) Bound the retry: `#respawn` should not spin forever on a requirement no host can ever satisfy -- it should surface a blocker the way factions does for the 80 GB SingularityFn3 wall (shared/strategy/factions/decide.ts:379), so the run fails loudly instead of going quiet. Doing (2) alone would turn a silent stall into a diagnosable one without unblocking the leg.
openDefects.cause: TWO defects in `game/lib/ns-proxy.ts`, compounding. (1) `#guaranteeFit` capped what it ASKED for at MAX_ASK_GB (64) while demanding the uncapped priced sum, so the arena reserved 65.6 GB for a respawn that would accept nothing under 162.1 GB -- ask and demand could never meet. (2) `priceCall` returned the 80 GB `UNKNOWN_CALL_GB` fallback whenever `getFunctionRamCost` threw, which includes the transient case where `nsMain()` is momentarily unpublished (it is, across a prestige -- the first 162.1 GB demand lands in the same instant as the third install). The union sums that guess once PER member, so the two-path dnet `guaranteeFit` demanded 2 x 80 = 160 GB for calls that really cost 0.05 and 1.3 GB.
openDefects.whyItIsADeadlock: The controller needs the placement to act; the placement needs free fleet RAM; freeing it means buying a bigger server, which is `hacking:infrastructure:ram` wanting $3.16t and DENIED (`reason: outbid`, `available: 0`) while stock holds the bankroll as working capital; and issuing that purchase requires the controller, which is blocked. Nothing in the loop can break the cycle, which is why it survives to a 120h horizon.
openDefects.fix: `priceOf` now reports whether the runtime actually gave a price, so a GUESS can inform the ask but never becomes an unsatisfiable floor; a partly-guessed union is held to what a resident can be granted, while a fully-priced one keeps its floor however large, because those calls genuinely cannot run in less. `#guaranteeFit` now raises the ask to cover its own floor. And `#respawn` gained the failure exit it never had: a minute of unbroken refusal is declared impossible and throws, emitting `proxy.impossible`, so a demand the fleet cannot meet becomes a fault a feature can report instead of a silent halt that takes the whole controller with it. Pinned by tests/ns-proxy.test.ts and tests/ram-budget.test.ts.

openDefects.nextStep: Two things, in this order. (1) Re-measure the capped fix from a committed tree; if 9 installs / 40 augmentations reproduces, it is a headline. (2) The leg is still BOUND by this leg however the derivative is priced -- the reputation grind is 46-54h on the seeds that take it against 11h for the seeds that donate. The question worth asking next is not how reputation is priced but why two seeds in three fail to reach the donation branch, which is a money question: `donationSec` charges `rep * dollarsPerRep - money` against `moneyPerSec`, so the branch is chosen by income, and BN4 nerfs every income channel except stocks and contracts.
openDefects.suspectedMispricing: UNCONFIRMED, from reading rather than measurement, and recorded so the next pass starts here. `perturbedRates` (shared/strategy/progression/marginal.ts) is the derivative every channel's worth is taken with, and six of its seven resources substitute their declared fallback when nothing has been measured yet -- `rates.moneyPerSec > 0 ? rates.moneyPerSec : FALLBACK_MONEY_PER_SEC` and so on. `reputation` is the exception: it scales `daedalusRepPerSec` and `gangRepPerSec` as they stand, so on a run that has never worked for Daedalus it scales zero by 1.01 and the perturbation moves the route ETA not at all -- even though the ETA itself priced that leg at FALLBACK_DAEDALUS_REP_PER_SEC. The slope is then taken at a different operating point from the value. `operatingRate` in the same file likewise returns `undefined` for reputation where every other resource answers, so the published marginal carries no `atRatePerSec` for the one channel the route is bound by. Both are the circular starvation the file's own comments describe having already fixed for money. NOT YET SHOWN to change the leg: the marginal has a floor that catches the zero slope, so the worth is not zero, only coarse. Measure the A/B before changing it.
openDefects.status: PARTLY FIXED 2026-08-30 (the derivative), with regression tests; the leg is still bound by this leg
openDefects.assumedCauseRefuted: MEASURED, and it was wrong. The nextStep carried over from bn1.json said 'factions loses the slot'. It does not: on a telemetry-on leg-bn4.1 seed-1 run, `arbitration.slot` names factions in 53,987 of 82,631 state records and career in 28,644 -- factions holds Player.currentWork 65% of the time. The leg reads `measured: false` because DAEDALUS specifically has not been joined and worked before the horizon, so `trackers.daedalusRep` is still zero. That is a fact about how late the invite gate falls, not a lost auction, and the BN1 note should be re-checked the same way before it is believed there either.
openDefects.cause: The reputation channel was the only live one whose worth came from the coarse all-parts FLOOR rather than from a perturbation. `perturbedRates` (shared/strategy/progression/marginal.ts) scaled `rates.daedalusRepPerSec` -- the MEASURED tracker, zero until Daedalus is worked -- while `eta.ts` priced the leg from `daedalusRepPerSecProjected`, the driver's formula projection. Zero times 1.01 is zero, so the estimate did not move and the slope was taken with respect to a variable the value does not use. Six of the seven resources already substitute their declared fallback here (`rates.moneyPerSec > 0 ? rates.moneyPerSec : FALLBACK_MONEY_PER_SEC` and so on); reputation was the exception. `operatingRate` likewise answered `undefined` for reputation alone, so the published marginal carried no `atRatePerSec` for the one channel the route is bound by.
openDefects.evidenceForCause: The published marginal, read straight off a telemetry run at t=18.68h: reputation `{state: estimated, secondsPerRelativeRate: 102241, horizon: "future-binding"}` with NO `atRatePerSec`, beside hacking `{... horizon: "node", atRatePerSec: 0.0172}` and money `{... atRatePerSec: 3.4e6}`. `future-binding` is this module's own label for 'neither perturbation moved, so the floor was used', and 102,241 is exactly `linearSecondsPerRelativeRate` of the 28.68h leg.
openDefects.fix: `perturbedRates` now scales the measured-or-projected-or-declared rate the ETA itself priced with, and `operatingRate` answers for reputation (the gang stream on the gang route, Daedalus otherwise), so the published marginal carries its operating point like every other channel. AND a discontinuity cap, which the first attempt needed and did not have: `routeEtas` chooses between discrete branches -- grind the reputation or donate for it -- and a 1% rate change that FLIPS that branch moves the estimate by the whole branch difference, which `/ delta` then multiplies by a hundred. Uncapped, that made reputation out-bid every other use of the work slot and STALLED a leg seed outright (3-seed batch, seed 1: 16 augmentations, hacking 3 for the 7.8h after its last install, a 4,498h route ETA). The perturbed slope is now capped at the linear reading of the resource's own legs -- a 1% faster rate is worth at most 1% of the time that rate governs -- which also means the new worth can only be LOWER than the old floor, never higher. Pinned by tests/marginal.test.ts, two of whose cases fail on the old code.
openDefects.legVerdict: MEASURED, and NOT carried into the headline numbers. A 3-seed 24h batch with the capped fix produced seed 2 at 9 installs / 40 augmentations -- better than ANY seed of the 2026-08-30 batch on both counts (8 / 38) -- and seed 1 comparable at 6 installs / 31 augs; route ETAs were worse (39.66h and 46.91h against 24.99h). Seed 3 reached 26.76 GB RSS at 23.6h and was killed by an external cap. Those numbers are NOT promoted, because the tree they were taken on also carried another session's uncommitted simulator work (output retention, a memory budget in pumpGuard, run summaries), so they are not attributable and not reproducible from a commit. Re-measure from a clean tree before moving `bestAugmentationsAt24Hours`.
openDefects.knownEdgeOfTheFix: REPORTED BY REVIEW AND LEFT AS IS, because the alternative reopens what the cap closed. The discontinuity cap is `linearSecondsPerRelativeRate(max(installResourceSec, nodeResourceSec))`, so it is ZERO when the route has no leg labelled with the resource -- and the Daedalus route reaches exactly that state once Daedalus favor crosses the donation threshold: `donateParts` becomes the single `daedalus reputation donation` part, which is labelled `money`, and reputation has no labelled seconds at all. Reputation is then priced at a measured zero with `reason: "the selected plan has no dependency on this resource"`, even where a rate change large enough to flip the branch back to grinding would genuinely move the estimate. VERIFIED by reading eta.ts, NOT yet observed in a measured run: the 2026-08-30 batches that took the donation route were all on the LOCKED branch, which does carry a `daedalus favor unlock reputation` part. Exempting the zero-legs case would restore the mirror-image hundredfold branch flip in the other direction, so the honest reading is that on the unlocked branch the route's marginal path IS money and a zero is the right answer -- with one caveat worth checking if reputation ever looks starved there: `channelWorth` lets a measured marginal OVERRIDE a posted `factionRep` need for the same currency, so a rep requirement at some faction the route does not model would be silenced by this zero.

openDefects.whyItSurfacedNow: Probably not new. Before the ns-proxy fix these runs wedged at ~21h and coasted doing almost nothing, so they never reached the memory the working controller needs. A run that actually keeps deciding for 24 virtual hours is a much heavier run.
openDefects.nextStep: None for memory. The throughput decay it rode on is still open -- see openDefects/cost-grows-with-run-length.
diagnosis: MEASURED, not inferred. `--cost` now samples process RSS, live processes and servers every interval, and `SIM_COST_DETAIL=<n>` adds a bun:jsc heap census. Three readings decided it.

(1) IT IS NOT A RETENTION LEAK. On a healthy 30h seed-3 run the LIVE heap oscillates between 50 MB and 450 MB and comes back every time, while RSS ratchets to 2.05 GB; live processes stay in 20-4,200 and servers in 74-137 for the whole run. Nothing the simulator owns grows without bound.

(2) IT IS A COLLECTION THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. On the seed that blows up, the same census reads live=1,873 MB then live=12,863 MB then live=21,374 MB in three consecutive 30s samples, with heap CAPACITY tracking it -- 14.6 million array/object backing stores allocated with no sweep in between. The heap was not leaking, it was uncollected.

(3) THE PACING WAS PRICED IN THE WRONG CLOCK. `Clock.runAsync` forced a full collection every 10 VIRTUAL minutes, floored at 2 wall seconds. Garbage is produced by HOST WORK. Those agree only while throughput is steady, and this leg's throughput decays by an order of magnitude across its horizon (8.06 -> 0.12 virtual hours per wall minute, seed 3), so the same 10 virtual minutes stretches from under a second of allocation to minutes of it. It is self-reinforcing: a bigger heap makes every pass slower, which stretches the interval further -- the OOM spiral sim/clock.ts already names for the zero-delay stall.

That is also why it looked seed-specific and machine-specific. The same seed 2 blew up to 22 GB while sharing the machine with two other sims and survived at 1.87 GB alone: contention does not change the trajectory (the runs agree cycle for cycle) but it changes how much wall time -- and therefore how much allocation -- fits inside 10 virtual minutes. The reported crashes came from `bench:sim:leg-bn4.1`, which runs three seeds CONCURRENTLY, i.e. under maximum contention.
openDefects.fix: `CollectionPacer` (sim/clock.ts) bounds the interval on the resource itself: RSS GROWTH since the last collection is the primary trigger -- it is what actually kills the process and it assumes nothing about how fast a phase allocates -- with the virtual-time trigger kept as the cheap common case, a wall ceiling backstopping a host that reports no RSS, and the 2-second floor kept because it is what stops a fast simulator spending its wall clock inside synchronous collections. The baseline is re-read AFTER collecting, so a collection that frees nothing cannot re-arm the trigger into a loop. It cannot change what a run decides: there is no `WeakRef` or `FinalizationRegistry` anywhere in the tree, so nothing observes collection. Pinned by sim/tests/clock.test.ts, whose central case is a run whose virtual clock has crawled -- the exact shape the old rule missed.
openDefects.result: `bench:sim:leg-bn4.1` at 24h: 3/3 seeds valid and COMPLETED, peak RSS 1.02 / 1.71 / 2.50 GB, in 27 wall minutes for the batch. Before the pacer the same seed 2 under the same concurrency passed 22 GB at t=21.0h and was killed. This is the first end-to-end verification the leg has had.
openDefects.reopenedNote: 2026-08-30, LATER THE SAME DAY: the pacer bounds the PACING failure it was built for -- the 3-seed batch it was verified on ran 3/3 at 1.02/1.71/2.50 GB -- but it does not bound every path to a huge LIVE set, and two later batches found one. A batch carrying the (refused) pooling change had seed 2 reach 55.85 GB with 5,971 live processes; a batch carrying the reputation fix plus another session's in-flight simulator work had seed 3 reach 26.76 GB at 23.6h. Both were killed by an external RSS cap rather than segfaulting, which is the pacer's instruments doing their job, but the defect class is not closed: when the live set genuinely grows, collecting more often cannot help. The live-process count is the number to watch -- it is on every `--cost` sample now, and 5,971 against a normal 100-1,500 is what named the pooling change as the cause in that batch.

openDefects.status: OPEN, cause found and attributed; the available repair is measured and REFUSED
openDefects.what: leg-bn4.1 gets steadily more expensive to simulate as it runs: throughput falls -55% to -78% across a 3-seed 24h batch, and on a 30h seed-3 probe at 45c2d062 it fell from 8.06 to 0.12 virtual hours per wall minute -- 67x within one run.
evidence: `--cost` throughput curve on all three seeds of the 24h batch, and the 30h seed-3 probe.
It is NOT the world growing: live processes stay in 20-4,200 and servers in 74-137 across a whole 30h run, both bounded and both oscillating rather than climbing.

The decayed phases come in BURSTS of allocation rather than a steady grind -- a single 30s sample at 20.2h held 4.8M Function, 558k JSLexicalEnvironment, 199k ProxyObject and 117k Promise objects, then the next sample was back to a tenth of that. Something re-decides at frame rate for seconds at a time.
Per-interval Netscript deltas (SIM_COST_DETAIL) in those bursts are led by `atExit` and `exec` -- 104,807 and 78,547 in one 30s interval at 17.9h -- so the churn is process launches, not planning.
openDefects.whyItMatters: It is not only host cost. The route ETAs say this leg is 49-106h long, and at the tail throughput a 100h leg is many wall hours. Until this is fixed, `reached: true` is not reachable in a batch anyone will sit through.
openDefects.nextStep: Make the reuse test DEMAND-bound before re-trying it. Pooling shrinks the process population only when a pooled worker's SHAPE matches the next job; the current test uses the aggregate steady-state period `weakenMs / depth` at the CAPACITY-bound depth, which is optimistic on any farm that never fills its pipeline -- jit-fragmentation runs at 91% idle RAM and still passes it. Where it is wrong the pooled and one-shot populations grow at the same time, which is what 5,971 live processes is.
itIsTwoThings: SEPARATED by the per-interval instruments. `cycles/vh` is a flat 18,000 all run (200 ms engine cycles, as it must be), so the denominator is honest.

(1) NOT A PATHOLOGY: `events/vh` grows about 5x, 47,505 -> 299,323 on seed 3. The farm gets bigger, so the simulation genuinely has more to do. `us/event` is FLAT at 150-330us across that whole stretch, which is what says the growth is work rather than waste. The world is not leaking: live processes stay in 20-4,200 and servers in 74-137 for a whole 30h run.

(2) THE PATHOLOGY: `us/event` then explodes late -- from ~21.8h on seed 2 it goes 1157, 776, 1441, 1081, 4324us against the 200-300 it held all run. That is cost per unit of work, not more work. The collection pacer cut the worst of it (peak 4324us before, 1465us after) but did not remove it.
openDefects.cause: The residue is the farm launching a PROCESS PER OP because worker pooling is not engaging: `exec` per virtual hour grows 28,069 -> 153,460 and `atExit` 52,189 -> 183,388 over the same stretch, and those two lead every burst interval. That is the regression commit 7c265f39 already bisected and diagnosed but did not repair, and it is a MISPRICING: `jitRoles` books POOL_REUSE_WINDOW_MS (5 s) of extra slot hold on every unpooled role, which roughly triples the schedule envelope and halves the batch rate, while the gate that would turn pooling on required `liveProcessCount > POOL_PRESSURE_OPS` -- a process pressure only the pooled state can reach. The gate can only open from a state the gate itself prevents, and its own comment already marked the -20% measurement behind it UNVERIFIED and confounded.
openDefects.repairTriedAndRefused: Deleting the process-pressure term -- leaving `weakenMs / depth <= POOL_REUSE_WINDOW_MS`, which is the whole economic test -- DOES engage pooling: jit-one-server goes 12.100 -> 24.200 batches/s and $7.531276e9 -> $2.441402e10, past its recorded $1.30122e10, and the leg batch's slowest seed got 25% cheaper with one seed's throughput drift falling from -71% to -5%. It is NOT SHIPPED, because the leg refuses it: on a 3-seed 24h batch seed 2 reached 55.85 GB RSS with 5,971 live processes and had to be killed -- it reintroduces openDefects/memory-blowup-on-long-runs -- while seeds 1 and 3 finished with worse route ETAs (45.94h against 31.30h, 273.42h against 81.72h). See sim/tests/baselines/jit.json for the whole lane's before/after.
